summary: Sharon Salzberg works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at the University at Buffalo (~1969–1971) and trained under teachers including Anagarika Munindra, Dipa Ma, S. N. Goenka, Mahasi Sayadaw, Sayadaw U Pandita, and Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, co-founding the Insight Meditation Society.

Shashibhusan Dasgupta was an indologist and scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. Educated at Brojomohun College, Scottish Church College, and the University of Calcutta (MA ~1933–1935, PhD ~1937–1939), he served as a Lecturer at the University of Calcutta from ~1939 to 1964.

Shayne Clarke specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Bukkyo University, earned an MA at the University of Canterbury under Paul Harrison, and completed a PhD at UCLA under Gregory Schopen; he served as Associate Professor at McMaster University (attested 2015–2016).

Shechen Gyaltsab was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies figure. He studied under numerous teachers, including Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Patrul Rinpoche, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and taught Dilgo Khyentse and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.
Shechen Rabjam Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure. He studied under spiritual teacher Dilgo Khyentse and founded the organization Karuna-Shechen in 2000.

Sheila Jasanoff studied at Radcliffe College, the University of Bonn, Harvard University, and Harvard Law School. She held academic posts at Cornell University (~1978–1998) and as professor at Harvard University from ~1998.

Shek-wing Tam worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studying under Dudjom Rinpoche, Yingguang Qu, and Yui Chi Lau. He held a professorship at Renmin University of China and served on the Academic Advisory Board of the Faculty of Nationalist Studies at Tsinghua University.

Sheldon Pollock is an Indologist and linguist who studied at Harvard (~1967–1975) under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He held professorships at the University of Iowa, the University of Chicago, and Columbia University (~2005–2023).

Sheng Yen was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at Jing'an Temple Buddhist Academy and Rissho University. He held posts at Shandao Temple, National Cheng Kung University, and the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (~1985–2009).

Shenghai Li specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, where he studied under Donald R. Davis Jr., Charles Hallisey, and Gudrun Bühnemann, along with traditional teachers.

Shenpen Hookham is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at the University of Reading and earned a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Michael M. Broido, while also studying under Tibetan teachers including Kalu Rinpoche.
Shenpen Nangwa was a Tibetologist and Buddhist philosopher who studied under Patrul Rinpoche. He held a post at Dzogchen Monastery from ~1900 to 1927.

Sherab Gyatso was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied at Gori Dratsang, Detsha, Guru, Labrang, and Drepung Monasteries. He served as President of the Buddhist Association of China (~1953–1966) and Dean of the Buddhist Academy of China.

Sherry B. Ortner is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. She studied at Bryn Mawr College and the University of Chicago (PhD ~1970), later holding posts at Sarah Lawrence College, the University of Michigan, and the University of California, Los Angeles.
Sherry Chayat is a religious and Buddhist studies figure who studied at Vassar College and trained under Eido Tai Shimano (~1967–1998), whom she succeeded in 2011.

Shichang Ma was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He worked as a researcher in Buddhist archaeology at the Dunhuang Academy (1963–1978) and held a post in the Archaeology Department at Peking University beginning in 1982.
Shigeki Kaizuka worked in sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University from ~1925 to 1928 and later held a post there from ~1949 to 1968.

Shigeki Kudo is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts as an assistant (助手) at Kyoto University, and as an associate professor (助教授) at Shuchiin University and the International Buddhist University (attested 1972–1973).

Shigeki Moro specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Waseda, Toyo, and Kansai Universities, and held an associate professorship at Hanazono University (2002–2015) and a professorship at Waseda University (2025).
Shigemasa Fukui is a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at Waseda University from ~1955 to 1960 and later served as a professor (教授) there from ~1978 to 2006.
